@priscillz thank you for such a thorough response. It’s incredible to me that people can agree on so many things yet still fall on “opposite” sides. Most of the people I know in the anti abortion community, myself included, agree and advocate for, spend our time and money on ALL of the things you mentioned in your comment! Anti abortion pregnancy centers regularly address all of those concerns with their services. But we just also believe we should prioritize those things while not aborting babies. I think what stood out to me in your comments was discussing the “binary” and how you view this issue as a spectrum. I know that I do not view it as a spectrum! To me, the legality of abortion and the social net that cares for the women and families are two distinct debates. The social piece, what are we doing to support those in need, for sure is a spectrum (sex Ed, support of foster and adoption, parenting education, etc). But the act of the abortion to me is unavoidably binary. Is a woman pregnant with an innocent living human being? Yes. Should it be legal to kill innocent living human beings? No. So I think that makes a lot of sense to me and helps me to understand “the other side” a little bit better. Thanks for your time today.

The “pro-choice” designation is really deceiving. It sucks the left is so good at language and shaping culture. In reality, people who are pro-life are also pro-choice; we support women in caring for (“keeping”) their baby, in adoption, in abstinence, etc. The only thing we don’t support is murder. Whereas the only difference for societally labelled “pro-choice” people is that they advocate for murder (abortion). It should really just be pro-life, and pro-abortion.
